Thanks again for the call today - great discussion. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single thread to follow.

Call highlights:
- Goal: support multi-article summarization & cross-document Q&A inside a single user session (10k-50k tokens of context).
- Primary concerns: truncation behavior on long inputs, summarization fidelity across very long narratives, and regression risk when switching to quantized model variants.
- Current infra: Acme runs inference on a mix of CPU-heavy preprocessing + GPU inference; typical request sizes range from 20k tokens for research reports down to 2k for user notes.

Recommended models to evaluate (based on cost/latency tradeoffs we discussed):
- redwood-llama-70b-q8 (recommended starting point) - good long-context kernel support + quantized for cost savings
- redwood-long-13b-ctx32k (lower cost, 32k native context window) - good baseline for summarization experiments
- redwood-flan-xl-30b (higher quality for instruction-following; consider for final UX)

Benchmarks & artifacts I shared during the call:
- Eval dashboard (long-context family): https://redwood.app/evals/ACME-2027-42-long-context
- Prompt set (initial): Drive folder link (shared) - acme_long_context_prompt_set_v1.csv attached
- Redwood benchmark PDF: redwood-eval-benchmarks-20270425.pdf attached

Technical notes we covered:
- Truncation behavior: our runtime supports progressive KV caching and prefix retention. For models with native 32k windows we avoid truncation up to that limit; with quantized 70B variants we recommend chunked encoding + overlapping context to preserve important boundary info (Rishi cc'd can add specifics).
- Summarization fidelity: recommend two-stage eval - (1) extractive QA checks on gold highlights, (2) human-rated summaries on a stratified sample (short/medium/very long).
- Regression monitoring: set up per-prompt-set QA thresholds and a rollout policy (canary -> 25% -> 100%). We can wire alerts to your Slack channel for drops > X% on key metrics.

Next steps (proposed timeline):
1) You share a representative subset of 50 long-docs + 20 edge-case shorter docs (drop in Drive link) - Acme to provide by EOD Thu (29 Apr).
2) We run the first-pass eval on redwood-llama-70b-q8 + redwood-long-13b-ctx32k (3 business days).
3) Quick sync to review results and pick a final candidate for UX testing (follow-up meeting - 30-45 minutes).

Please confirm if timeline looks good and whether we should include anyone else from your side (engineering/infra).

Adding some technical detail on truncation and chunking approach so Alex has the specifics. 

- Native-32k models (e.g., redwood-long-13b-ctx32k): single-pass attention to 32k tokens - lowest latency for a given end-to-end request because we avoid chunk stitching. For a 20k token request latency we typically see 600-900ms p95 on p4d-equivalent infra (numbers on our eval dashboard).
- Quantized 70B (redwood-llama-70b-q8): we support a chunked pipeline where we split inputs into overlapping chunks (e.g., 8k chunks with 256-token overlap), run attention per-chunk while preserving KV cache across chunks. That adds ~20-40% overhead compared to native-32k on long requests, but cost-per-token is lower due to q8 memory footprint enabling higher throughput.
- Truncation behavior: if you exceed model max context we can configure: (A) sliding-window chunking with summary-state (retain compressed summaries of earlier chunks in KV), (B) prioritized-prefix retention (keep most recently referenced sections), or (C) failure/400 with guidance to client (not recommended). Option (A) is the default we use for summarization tasks to preserve global coherence.
- Regression risk with quantized variants: quality delta is workload-dependent. For extractive QA we see minimal regression (<=2-3% F1) on our benchmarks; for abstractive summarization, human-rated ROUGE/LLM-based faithfulness metrics can show larger deltas. We recommend running a head-to-head on your gold highlights before rolling out.

Pricing ballpark for the 3-day eval (very rough):
- redwood-long-13b-ctx32k: $850-1,200 total (depending on run concurrency)
- redwood-llama-70b-q8: $1,400-2,000 total (higher GPU runtime but fewer runs due to throughput)
- We can also do a capped-engagement (flat fee) if you prefer predictable billing - happy to have sales follow up with a proposal.
